title: Inspecting and Forwarding Mixin Content knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Inspecting and Forwarding Mixin Content” in Dart Sass?
options: Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles.
questions.explanation: A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Content-existence checks”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
For content-existence checks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
questions.answer_key: For content-existence checks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.explanation: For content-existence checks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Inspecting and Forwarding Mixin Content”?
options: Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.
questions.answer_key: Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly.
questions.explanation: Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
